title: The Local Clinic
description:
Sore throat for a few days.
ENT clinic down the street. Checked in, waited ten minutes.

Three-minute consultation, prescription in hand, straight to the pharmacy next door.
Korean healthcare is fast. And cheap.

choices.text: Fill the prescription and grab some vitamins while you're there
choices.result_text:
Pharmacy: ₩4,800. Consultation: ₩4,500. Vitamins: ₩8,000.

Foreign friends wouldn't believe these prices.
National health insurance makes it possible. I use it like it's nothing — but it isn't.

choices.text: Just get the prescription — minimize cost
choices.result_text:
Consultation ₩4,500, meds ₩4,800 — ₩9,300 total.

Learned something: in this country, go to the clinic immediately when you're sick.
Waiting it out costs more.

title: Year-End Tax Settlement
description:
January — the company sends a request for year-end tax settlement documents.
NTS Hometax opens with a long list of deduction categories.

Medical expenses, tuition, card spending, monthly rent...
How much you get back depends on how carefully you claim them.

choices.result_text:
Monthly rent tax credit, card income deduction, medical expenses — all of it.
Refund estimate: ₩150,000.

Money the government owes you. If you're too lazy to claim it, it just disappears.
People who know this system keep more.

choices.text: Assume the company handles it — submit the basics
choices.result_text:
Just filed the basics. Refund estimate: ₩0.

Found out later — just claiming the rent credit would have gotten back hundreds of thousands.
Next year, I'll do it properly.

title: Health Insurance Bill
description:
KakaoPay notification: health insurance bill arrived.
Locally insured (not through employer). No income, but it pulls out every month.

When I had a job, the company covered half.
Now I'm unemployed — I pay all of it.

choices.result_text:
₩89,000. One click and it's gone.

The insurance is why clinic visits are cheap.
I know that. Still — ₩89,000 is a lot when you're not earning.

choices.text: Look into an installment payment plan
choices.result_text:
Opened the health insurance app. Installment payment: available.
Can split into three payments.

That one application bought a month of breathing room.
The system gives you as much as you know to ask for.

title: Jeonse Contract
description:
Sitting at the real estate office.
A jeonse contract.

Jeonse only exists in Korea.
Pay 60–80% of the property value as a deposit — and live there rent-free.

Foreign friends take a while to understand how that works.

choices.text: Get the fixed-date stamp and register the lease — cover all bases
choices.result_text:
Pulled the registry, checked for prior claims, got the fixed-date stamp, registered the leasehold.
The agent said 'you really know your stuff.'

If the tenant doesn't protect themselves, this money can vanish.
In Korea's jeonse system, knowledge is survival.

The agent handled it. I signed the documents.

Checked afterward — the fixed-date stamp required a separate trip to the community center.
Luckily caught it in time. Jeonse fraud isn't just something that happens to other people.

title: Convenience Store Interview
description:
Part-time job posting. ₩9,860/hr — minimum wage.
Includes four major insurances plus weekly holiday pay, so the effective rate is a little higher.

The store manager skimmed my resume.
'Are you currently working any other part-time jobs?' First question.

choices.result_text:
Hired. 6 AM to 11 AM shift.

First time I'd seen Seoul at dawn. Office workers heading out, students heading to school.
The convenience store is the capillary of Korea's 24-hour society. I worked at the very end of it.

Thought about it, then said no.

On this hourly rate, I'd barely breathe. I need something that builds toward something.
I don't have that yet. And while I look, the bank account shrinks.
